headline: Security firm Horizon3.ai used Anthropic's Mythos AI model to find a critical flaw in Rejetto HFS, an open-source file server, and security firm VulnCheck now reports probes aimed at it.
score_reason: Kept at 5: a concrete flaw with scanning reported, though only probing and not confirmed breaches.
importance_line: Operators of Rejetto HFS file servers face probes for the flaw, and the case shows AI models finding flaws that attackers then probe, but no successful attacks are reported.
source: Security Affairs, citing VulnCheck and Horizon3
summary: Security Affairs reports, citing VulnCheck and Horizon3, that the flaw, CVE-2026-61500 (severity score 9.3), lets an attacker forge admin session cookies and run code on Rejetto HFS 3.x servers because the software built its cookie-signing key from a predictable random-number generator; it was published on 13 Jul 2026 and VulnCheck says it began detecting probes for it. Horizon3 says Mythos linked several weaknesses into a working attack path, while VulnCheck so far reports probing rather than confirmed breaches.
notes: SC Media page blocked (HTTP 403); written from Security Affairs. Tech Times (URL dated 5 Oct 2026) says exploitation began within 24 hours of disclosure and is only the second in-the-wild case from Project Glasswing; those claims conflict with the 13 Jul 2026 publication date and were not used. Security Affairs's headline says 'exploiting' but its text describes probes.
